notes: The single ye of Hearken ye all Judah stands after the imperative and is the verb's subject pronoun, while the ye of ye inhabitants stands before the noun and is the vocative's (rule 36).
לָכֶם and לֵאלֹהִים are each rendered inside a single English genitive, so the preposition fuses with the word holding the lexeme and the copula joins the fused unit (rule 49's closing sentences).
